svg.aria-label: Emulated Lab workflow: nine steps from prerequisites to a traffic report, plus the AI assistant
svg.text: Emulated Lab Workflow
Termwright runs real switch images under QEMU on your own Linux KVM hosts. These are the steps from an empty host to a traffic report,
and the AI assistant can do steps 2 to 9 for you.
Prepare the host and the image
Prerequisites
qcow2
Check these before you start.
A Linux host with KVM, reachable over SSH
Termwright on your computer
A switch image (.iso or .qcow2), or download one
Add a lab host
SSH
Open the Emulated Lab and add your host in Hosts.
Set Up installs QEMU after showing you the commands
No agent or service is needed on the host
Add more hosts to spread the lab across them
Pick an appliance
Choose what your virtual switches will run.
Ready templates from the public vendor list
Import a GNS3 appliance file
Reuse one template for as many switches as you need
Build the lab and send traffic
Get the disk image
qcow2
Every appliance needs a qcow2 disk.
Download a ready qcow2 image
Or install from your ISO and save a qcow2 disk
Reuse one image for many switches
Build the topology
T1
T2
T1
T2
Draw the network on the canvas.
Drag switches onto the canvas and cable their ports
Add test ports to send and receive traffic
Power everything on and open each console
Create traffic streams
voice EF
video AF41
IMIX data
T1
T2
Send traffic between the lab's test ports.
Create streams or reuse saved ones
Voice, video and mixed-size (IMIX) traffic with DSCP
Watch live rates, loss and latency
Analyse, capture and scale up
Analyse and save
Report
PASS
PASS
FAIL
See in one view whether the network passed.
Pass or fail per stream, with loss, latency and jitter
Limits such as maximum loss decide the result
Save the report as an HTML file
Capture and replay
.pcap
Record real traffic and play it back.
Capture packets on any cable (right-click the cable)
Open the .pcap file in the packet viewer
Replay a .pcap file into the lab as a stream
Line rate with TRex (optional)
TRex server
T1
T2
test ports in the lab
An optional engine for high-rate testing.
A TRex server sends the traffic
Its ports appear as test ports in the lab
Use it when the built-in engines are not fast enough
Or let the AI assistant do it for you
AI
Describe the goal
Ask in plain language, in Termwright or from your own AI app.
Works with the built-in assistant and, through MCP, other AI apps
Lab changes don't ask each time, but are recorded and can be reverted
AI
For example, you say
“Build two switches, cable them, send voice and video traffic
between them and give me the report.”
It builds the topology, powers it on and checks the cabling
It runs the streams and returns the pass or fail report
